{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Check for duplicates in patient_id
patient_id_counts = df['patient_id'].value_counts()
duplicate_patients = patient_id_counts[patient_id_counts > 1]

print(f"Number of patients with multiple records: {len(duplicate_patients)}")
print(f"Duplicate patient IDs: {list(duplicate_patients.index)}")

# Check sample_seq for each duplicate patient to confirm which row to keep
duplicate_rows = df[df['patient_id'].isin(duplicate_patients.index)]
duplicate_rows_sorted = duplicate_rows.sort_values(by=['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False])

# Keep only the row with the highest sample_seq for each patient
# This is the rule stated in the data dictionary
df_deduped = duplicate_rows_sorted.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Verify that no duplicates remain
final_counts = df_deduped['patient_id'].value_counts()
assert (final_counts == 1).all(), "Duplicates still exist after deduplication"

print(f"Final number of unique patients: {len(df_deduped)}")"}
